第64章 降维打击，昔日校花的消息-《重生2000：撕了协议我暴富了》

凌晨两点。

弄堂口的风透着黄浦江的潮气。

折叠桌底下滚了十几个空酒瓶。

张虎第一次没喝过林川。

大城市自带的压力，酒还没上桌人就先醉了三分。

他大着舌头，拍着胸脯：“川子……嗝，你看着，老子早晚在上海滩混出个人样！”

林川笑着没说话，把最后一口散啤喝完，起身结账。

他在路边拦了辆出租车，把晕乎乎的张虎塞进后座。

关车门前，林川顺手从张虎口袋里摸出那个屏幕裂了的诺基亚。

翻出外高桥那批货的单号和联系人短信，转发到自己手机上。

再把手机塞回张虎兜里，拍了拍车门。

“师傅，虹口区大连路。”

出租车尾灯消失在弄堂口。

林川站在路灯底下，掏出手机，拨通了苏晚棠的电话。

响了三声。

“林总。”苏晚棠的声音干脆利落，没有一丁点睡意。

“记个柜号。”

林川报了一串数字。

“外高桥保税区的。明天早上八点前，我要这批货正常上船。”

他停了半秒。

“另外，查一下是谁扣的。让他明白，张江的规矩，也管得到外高桥。”

“明白。”

电话挂断。

林川把手机揣进口袋，转身走出弄堂。

次日上午十点。

大连路一处出租屋。

张虎被一阵刺耳的手机铃声吵醒。宿醉让他脑壳里跟有人拿锤子敲似的。

他闭着眼摸到手机，按下接听，没好气地吼了一嗓子。

“谁啊？大清早的叫魂呢！”

那头安静了一秒。

紧接着，一个抖得跟筛糠的声音传了过来。

“张、张总？我是外高桥码头的刘主管啊！”

张虎愣了一下。

这名字他得转两圈才想起来——就是那个扣了他三个星期货、每次打电话都牛逼哄哄让他“等通知”的王八蛋。

上周他求这位刘主管吃饭，人家直接挂了他的电话。

此刻，刘主管的声音带着哭腔。

“张总，您现在在哪儿啊？求您赶紧来趟码头吧！放行手续我全给您办好了，就差您一个签字！”

张虎的酒瞬间醒了一半。

“你说什么？”

“放行了张总！货都装船了！您快来签个字，船等着开呢！”

张虎光着脚从床上蹦下来，连袜子都没穿就往裤腿里钻。

四十分钟后。

外高桥码头。

张虎站在集装箱堆场边上，整个人是懵的。

不仅那批被扣了三个星期的货柜已经装船完毕。

连这二十多天的滞箱费、港杂费——总共快两万块——全免了。

一分不收。

干净得不正常。

更不正常的是人。

那个卡了他脖子整整三个星期的海关科长，此刻正站在集装箱办公室门口。

Two o'clock in the morning.

The wind at the entrance of the alley carries the moisture of the Huangpu River.

A dozen empty wine bottles rolled under the folding table.

This is the first time Zhang Hu has ever drank Lin Chuan.

Big cities come with their own pressure, and people are already drunk before the wine is even served on the table.

He stuck out his tongue and patted his chest: "Kawako... Hiccup, look at me, sooner or later I will make a difference in Shanghai!"

Lin Chuan smiled without saying anything, drank the last sip of loose beer, and stood up to pay the bill.

He stopped a taxi on the side of the road and put the dizzy Zhang Hu into the back seat.

Before closing the car door, Lin Chuan took out the Nokia with a cracked screen from Zhang Hu's pocket.

He dug out the order number and contact text message of the Waigaoqiao shipment and forwarded it to his mobile phone.

He stuffed the phone back into Zhang Hu's pocket and patted the car door.

"Master, Dalian Road, Hongkou District."

The taxi's taillight disappeared at the entrance of the alley.

Lin Chuan stood under the street lamp, took out his mobile phone and dialed Su Wantang's number.

It rang three times.

"Mr. Lin." Su Wantang's voice was crisp and clear, without any hint of sleepiness.

"Remember the counter number."

Lin Chuan reported a series of numbers.

"It's from the Waigaoqiao Free Trade Zone. I want this batch of goods to be on board before eight o'clock tomorrow morning."

He paused for half a second.

"In addition, find out who dunked the ball. Let him understand that Zhangjiang's rules also apply to Waigaoqiao."

"Understood."

The phone hangs up.

Lin Chuan put his cell phone in his pocket, turned around and walked out of the alley.

Ten o'clock the next morning.

A rental house on Dalian Road.

Zhang Hu was awakened by the harsh ringtone of his cell phone.The hangover made his head feel like someone was hitting it with a hammer.

He touched the phone with his eyes closed, pressed answer, and roared angrily.

"Who is it? The soul is screaming so early in the morning!"

There was silence on the other end for a second.

Immediately afterwards, a shaking voice came over.

"Zhang, Mr. Zhang? I am Manager Liu from Waigaoqiao Pier!"

Zhang Hu was stunned for a moment.

He had to spin around twice before he remembered the name - it was the bastard who had withheld his goods for three weeks and always coaxed him to "wait for notification" every time he called.

Last week, he begged Manager Liu for a meal, but he immediately hung up on him.

At this moment, Manager Liu's voice was filled with tears.

"Mr. Zhang, where are you now? Please come to the pier quickly! I have completed all the release procedures for you, all I need is your signature!"

Zhang Hu was half sober in an instant.

"What did you say?"

"Let Mr. Zhang go! The goods are all loaded on the ship! Come and sign quickly, the ship is waiting to leave!"

Zhang Hu jumped off the bed with bare feet and slipped into his trousers without even wearing socks.

Forty minutes later.

Waigaoqiao Pier.

Zhang Hu stood at the edge of the container yard, completely confused.

Not only the containers that had been detained for three weeks have been shipped.

Even the demurrage fees and port miscellaneous fees for these more than 20 days - a total of nearly 20,000 yuan - are all waived.

Not a penny charged.

Abnormally clean.

Even more abnormal are people.

The customs section chief who had stuck his neck for three weeks was standing at the door of the container office.
